svg.text: Combined BTB + 2-bit counter in one dual-port RAM: port A read at fetch, port B written when a branch resolves
port A: synchronous read (fetch) · port B: write (update)
index = addr[9:2] → 256 sets, no associativity, no aliasing check
tag = addr[19:10] → addresses above bit 19 alias onto the same entry
a false hit is corrected at decode, a wrong target at execute
a miss predicts not-taken but is entered as weakly not-taken,
so one taken resolution is enough to flip it
tag of the address that was looked up
taken → next_pc = predicted target; the prediction travels with the
instruction to decode and execute for later verification
UPDATE (port B — one write per cycle)
BTB hit on a non-branch PC:
2-bit saturating counter — signed encoding, taken while strength ≥ 0
unconditional jumps update with previous strength 2'b01 so they stay strongly taken
misaligned branch targets are not written back to the BTB
tag compare; taken prediction redirects the PC (1 bubble)
branch resolved against the carried prediction
BTB and counter written; mispredict resteers the front end
